text.p: Italian debt markets ended down along with other markets after Btps and futures rode out a couple of tense days on the home political front.
Analysts were digesting the upshot of a government struggle to get parliamentary backing for sending forces to Albania.

Although they expected the government to survive forthcoming confidences votes in both parliamentary houses, confidence was not overwhelming on the longer term effectiveness of the current centre-left coalition.
The June LIFFE futures contract was 58 basis points down at 127.17 with support at 127.00.
The February 2007 Btp ended 58 basis points lower at 94.22, with a yield of 7.73 percent and a spread over the 10-year Bund of 183 basis points.

The lira wobbled slightly on brief concern stemming from a news report that plans may be afoot to persuade Italy not to be in EMU wave one. But traders said interest quickly subsided with no facts to back the idea and the lira recovered slightly from a dip to its ERM central parity of 990 per mark.
Instead players were looking at the long term prospects of Romano Prodi's government with one broker at an Italian bank saying bluntly: "This has damaged the government a lot."
"It's embarrassing that the government has to have an accord with the opposition, the cracks are definitely showing and there just isn't enough glue," the broker in London said.
Economists reckoned the government can limp on for a few months more but they see plenty of hurdles ahead when it comes to making welfare reforms and presenting the 1998 budget.

For now analysts say Btps should remain supported on the basis of economic fundamentals -- politics permitting -- with lower inflation expected in April and investors daring to hope for another Bank of Italy rate cut in the next month or so.
